title: MAHARASHTRA CLASS 12 — English | Narration Direct Indirect
description: Subject-wise test on Narration Direct Indirect (English) for MAHARASHTRA CLASS 12. 25Q.
subject: maha12-english

questions.question: Choose the correct indirect narration for the given sentence: Rina said, 'I am going to the market.'

options.text: Rina said that I was going to the market.
options.explanation: The pronoun 'I' should change to 'she' to refer to Rina in indirect speech.

options.text: Rina said that she is going to the market.
options.explanation: The tense should shift to past continuous ('was going') as the reporting verb is in the past tense.

options.text: Rina said that she was going to the market.
options.explanation: Correct pronoun change ('I' to 'she') and tense shift ('am going' to 'was going').

options.text: Rina said that I am going to the market.
options.explanation: Both the pronoun and tense should be adjusted in indirect speech.

questions.explanation: The reporting verb 'said' indicates past tense. The pronoun 'I' changes to 'she' to refer to Rina, and the present continuous tense 'am going' changes to past continuous 'was going'.
questions.hint: Check for pronoun and tense changes in indirect speech.
questions.subject: maha12-english

questions.question: Choose the correct indirect narration for the given sentence: The teacher said to the students, 'Be quiet.'

options.text: The teacher told the students that they should be quiet.
options.explanation: While grammatically correct, it does not use the most common reporting verbs for imperative sentences.

options.text: The teacher asked the students to be quiet.
options.explanation: Correct, but the question allows for multiple correct options.

options.text: The teacher ordered the students to be quiet.
options.explanation: Correct, but the question allows for multiple correct options.

options.text: Both B and C are correct depending on the context.
options.explanation: Both 'asked' and 'ordered' are valid reporting verbs for imperative sentences, depending on the tone used.

questions.explanation: Imperative sentences can be reported using verbs like 'asked', 'ordered', 'advised', 'requested' followed by an infinitive (to + verb). Both 'asked' and 'ordered' are suitable reporting verbs for 'Be quiet', depending on the tone.
questions.hint: Imperative sentences often use 'asked', 'ordered', or 'requested' in indirect speech.
questions.subject: maha12-english

questions.question: Choose the correct indirect narration for the given sentence: He said, 'I saw a movie yesterday.'

options.text: He said that he saw a movie the day before.
options.explanation: The tense should shift to past perfect ('had seen') when the reporting verb is in the past tense.

options.text: He said that he had seen a movie the day before.
options.explanation: Correct tense shift ('saw' to 'had seen') and adverb change ('yesterday' to 'the day before').

options.text: He said that he has seen a movie yesterday.
options.explanation: The tense should shift to past perfect, and 'yesterday' should change to 'the day before'.

options.text: He said that he saw a movie yesterday.
options.explanation: Both the tense and adverb should be adjusted in indirect speech.

questions.explanation: The simple past tense ('saw') in direct speech changes to past perfect tense ('had seen') in indirect speech. The time adverb 'yesterday' changes to 'the day before' or 'the previous day'.
questions.hint: Check for tense shift from simple past to past perfect in indirect speech.
questions.subject: maha12-english

questions.question: Choose the correct indirect narration for the given sentence: She asked me, 'When will you return the book?'

options.text: She asked me when I will return the book.
options.explanation: The auxiliary verb 'will' should change to 'would' in indirect speech.

options.text: She asked me when would I return the book.
options.explanation: The auxiliary verb 'would' should come after the subject ('I would'), not before.

options.text: She asked me when I would return the book.
options.explanation: Correct structure for indirect question: auxiliary verb ('would') after the subject ('I').

options.text: She asked me when I was returning the book.
options.explanation: The tense should shift to conditional ('would return'), not past continuous.

questions.explanation: In indirect questions, the reporting verb 'asked' is used. The interrogative word 'when' acts as a conjunction. The sentence structure changes from interrogative to assertive, so the auxiliary verb ('would') comes after the subject ('I'). 'Will' changes to 'would'.
questions.hint: In indirect questions, the auxiliary verb comes after the subject ('I would'), and 'will' changes to 'would'.
questions.subject: maha12-english

questions.question: Choose the correct indirect narration for the given sentence: My friend exclaimed, 'What a beautiful painting it is!'

options.text: My friend exclaimed that what a beautiful painting it was.
options.explanation: The sentence structure should change to assertive form ('it was a very beautiful painting').

options.text: My friend exclaimed that it is a very beautiful painting.
options.explanation: The tense should shift to past ('was') as the reporting verb is in the past tense.

options.text: My friend exclaimed what a beautiful painting it was.
options.explanation: The sentence should start with 'exclaimed that' to form a proper indirect speech structure.

options.text: My friend exclaimed with wonder that it was a very beautiful painting.
options.explanation: Correct reporting verb ('exclaimed with wonder') and tense shift ('is' to 'was').

questions.explanation: Exclamatory sentences are reported using verbs like 'exclaimed (with joy/sorrow/wonder)' and converted into assertive sentences. 'What a beautiful painting it is' becomes 'it was a very beautiful painting'.
questions.hint: Exclamatory sentences use 'exclaimed' and are converted to assertive sentences in indirect speech.
questions.subject: maha12-english

questions.question: Choose the correct indirect narration for the given sentence: The old man said, 'May God bless you!'

options.text: The old man said that God might bless me.
options.explanation: While grammatically correct, it does not use the most appropriate reporting verb for an optative sentence.

options.text: The old man prayed that God might bless me.
options.explanation: Correct reporting verb ('prayed') and modal shift ('may' to 'might').

options.text: The old man wished that God would bless me.
options.explanation: While grammatically correct, 'prayed' is more appropriate for a wish directed towards a divine entity.

options.text: The old man told me that God blesses me.
options.explanation: The tense and reporting verb are incorrect for an optative sentence.

questions.explanation: Optative sentences (expressing wishes or prayers) are reported using verbs like 'prayed', 'wished'. 'May' changes to 'might', and the sentence structure becomes assertive.
questions.hint: Optative sentences use 'prayed' or 'wished' in indirect speech, and 'may' changes to 'might'.
questions.subject: maha12-english

questions.question: Choose the correct indirect narration for the given sentence: 'If I were a bird, I would fly,' said the poet.

options.text: The poet said that if he was a bird, he would fly.
options.explanation: 'Were' should remain 'were' for unreal conditions in indirect speech.

options.text: The poet said that if he had been a bird, he would have flown.
options.explanation: This is a Type 3 conditional, but the original is Type 2 (unreal present). The tense should not shift to past perfect.

options.text: The poet said that if he were a bird, he would fly.
options.explanation: Correct retention of 'were' and 'would fly' for an unreal conditional sentence.

options.text: The poet said that if he is a bird, he would fly.
options.explanation: The tense in the 'if' clause should remain past ('were') for an unreal condition.

questions.explanation: For unreal or hypothetical conditional sentences (Type 2 and 3), the tense in the 'if' clause generally does not change in indirect speech if the condition remains unreal. 'Were' remains 'were', and 'would fly' remains 'would fly'.
questions.hint: In unreal conditional sentences, the tense in the 'if' clause does not change in indirect speech.
questions.subject: maha12-english

questions.question: Assertion (A): The sentence 'She said, 'I have completed my work.'' can be converted to indirect speech as 'She said that she had completed her work.' Reason (R): When the reporting verb is in the past tense, the present perfect tense in direct speech changes to past perfect tense in indirect speech.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Both the assertion and reason are correct, and the reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: The reason is the correct explanation for the assertion.

options.text: A is true, but R is false.
options.explanation: Both the assertion and reason are true.

options.text: A is false, but R is true.
options.explanation: The assertion is correct, and the reason supports it.

questions.explanation: The assertion correctly converts the sentence. The reason accurately states the rule for tense change from present perfect to past perfect when the reporting verb is in the past tense, directly explaining why the conversion in A is correct.
questions.hint: Check if the rule in the reason correctly explains the assertion.
questions.subject: maha12-english

questions.question: Read the following conversation and choose the correct indirect narration: Rohan: 'Where are you going, Manoj? I haven't seen you for ages!' Manoj: 'I'm going to the library. I was busy with my exams.'

options.text: Rohan asked Manoj where he was going and said that he hasn't seen him for ages. Manoj replied that he was going to the library and had been busy with his exams.
options.explanation: 'I haven't seen you for ages!' should be reported using 'exclaimed' and 'hadn't seen', not 'said' and 'hasn't seen'.

options.text: Rohan asked Manoj where he was going and added that he hadn't seen him for ages. Manoj replied that he was going to the library and was busy with his exams.
options.explanation: 'I haven't seen you for ages!' is an exclamation and should be reported with 'exclaimed', not 'added'.

options.text: Rohan asked Manoj where he was going and exclaimed that he hadn't seen him for ages. Manoj replied that he was going to the library and added that he had been busy with his exams.
options.explanation: Correct reporting verbs ('asked', 'exclaimed', 'replied', 'added'), pronoun changes, and tense shifts.

options.text: Rohan asked Manoj where he was going and said that he didn't see him for ages. Manoj replied that he is going to the library and was busy with his exams.
options.explanation: Incorrect reporting verb ('said' for an exclamation) and tense shifts ('didn't see' instead of 'hadn't seen', 'is going' instead of 'was going').

questions.explanation: 'Where are you going?' becomes 'where he was going.' 'I haven't seen you for ages!' is an exclamation, so 'exclaimed' is appropriate, and 'haven't seen' becomes 'hadn't seen.' 'I'm going to the library' becomes 'he was going to the library.' 'I was busy with my exams' is past simple, changing to past perfect 'had been busy' or can remain 'was busy' if the context implies ongoing past relevance.
questions.hint: Convert each part of the conversation separately, paying attention to pronouns, tenses, and reporting verbs.
questions.subject: maha12-english

questions.question: Choose the most accurate indirect narration for the statement: 'If I had known you were coming, I would have baked a cake,' said Mrs. Sharma.

options.text: Mrs. Sharma said that if she had known I was coming, she would have baked a cake.
options.explanation: While grammatically correct, it does not account for the strict tense shift of 'were coming' to 'had been coming'.

options.text: Mrs. Sharma said that if she knew I was coming, she would have baked a cake.
options.explanation: The 'if' clause should remain as Past Perfect ('had known'), not shift to simple past.

options.text: Mrs. Sharma said that if she had known I had been coming, she would have baked a cake.
options.explanation: Correct tense shift for the 'if' clause ('you were coming' to 'I had been coming') and retention of the main clause structure.

options.text: Mrs. Sharma said that if she had known I was coming, she would have baked a cake.
options.explanation: While plausible, it does not strictly follow the tense shift rule for the dependent clause.

questions.explanation: This is a Type 3 conditional sentence (unreal past). The 'if' clause (Past Perfect) and the main clause (would have + Past Participle) generally remain unchanged in indirect speech if the condition remains unreal. The dependent clause 'you were coming' (Past Continuous) needs to shift to Past Perfect Continuous ('had been coming').
questions.hint: For Type 3 conditionals, the 'if' clause and main clause remain unchanged, but the dependent clause may need a tense shift to Past Perfect Continuous.
questions.subject: maha12-english

questions.question: Choose the correct indirect speech for the given sentence: He said, "I am going to visit my grandparents tomorrow."

options.text: He said that he was going to visit his grandparents tomorrow.
options.explanation: The time expression 'tomorrow' should change to 'the next day' in indirect speech.

options.text: He said that he is going to visit his grandparents the next day.
options.explanation: The tense in direct speech ('am going') should change to past continuous ('was going') as the reporting verb is in the past tense.

options.text: He said that he was going to visit his grandparents the next day.
options.explanation: This option correctly changes the tense to past continuous, adjusts the pronoun from 'I' to 'he', and changes 'my' to 'his'. The time expression is correctly changed to 'the next day'.

options.text: He said that I was going to visit my grandparents the next day.
options.explanation: The pronoun 'I' should change to 'he' as it refers to the speaker in the direct speech.

questions.explanation: The present continuous tense ('am going') changes to past continuous ('was going'). The first-person pronoun 'I' changes to 'he' (referring to the speaker), and 'my' changes to 'his'. The time expression 'tomorrow' changes to 'the next day'.
questions.hint: Remember to change the tense and pronouns correctly.
questions.subject: maha12-english

questions.question: Convert the following sentence into indirect speech: The old woman asked the boy, "Where do you live?"

options.text: The old woman asked the boy where did he live.
options.explanation: The sentence structure should change from interrogative to assertive, so 'did he live' is incorrect here.

options.text: The old woman asked the boy where he lived.
options.explanation: This option correctly converts the interrogative sentence into an assertive one by using 'where he lived'.

options.text: The old woman asked the boy where he lives.
options.explanation: The tense should change to past tense ('he lived') because the reporting verb ('asked') is in the past.

options.text: The old woman asked the boy where do you live.
options.explanation: The pronoun 'you' should change to 'he' as it refers to the boy being addressed.

questions.explanation: For interrogative sentences starting with 'Wh' words, the 'Wh' word acts as the conjunction. The sentence structure changes from interrogative to assertive, so 'did he live' becomes 'he lived'. The simple present tense ('do you live') changes to simple past ('he lived').
questions.hint: Remember to change the question structure to an assertive sentence.
questions.subject: maha12-english

questions.question: Choose the correct indirect speech for the given sentence: The teacher said to the students, "Complete your assignments by Monday."

options.text: The teacher requested the students to complete their assignments by Monday.
options.explanation: 'Requested' is too mild for a command given by a teacher.

options.text: The teacher ordered the students to complete their assignments by Monday.
options.explanation: This option correctly uses 'ordered' to convert the imperative sentence into indirect speech and adjusts the pronoun 'your' to 'their'.

options.text: The teacher told the students that they should complete their assignments by Monday.
options.explanation: The sentence is a command, so 'told' with 'should' is less direct and less appropriate than 'ordered'.

options.text: The teacher asked the students if they would complete their assignments by Monday.
options.explanation: The sentence is a command, not a question, so 'asked if' is incorrect.

questions.explanation: Since it's an instruction or command from a teacher, 'said to' is best replaced by 'ordered'. The imperative mood is converted using 'to' + verb. 'Your' changes to 'their'.
questions.hint: Identify the type of speech (command/instruction) and choose the appropriate reporting verb.
questions.subject: maha12-english

questions.question: Convert the following into indirect speech: She said to him, "Have you finished reading the novel?"

options.text: She asked him if he had finished reading the novel.
options.explanation: This option correctly converts the yes/no question into an assertive sentence using 'if' and changes the tense to past perfect.

options.text: She asked him that if he had finished reading the novel.
options.explanation: 'That if' is grammatically incorrect; 'if' alone should be used as the conjunction.

options.text: She asked him whether you had finished reading the novel.
options.explanation: The pronoun 'you' should change to 'he' as it refers to the person being addressed.

options.text: She asked him if he has finished reading the novel.
options.explanation: The tense should change to past perfect ('had finished') because the reporting verb ('asked') is in the past.

questions.explanation: For yes/no questions, 'said to' changes to 'asked', and 'if' or 'whether' is used as a conjunction. The present perfect tense ('have you finished') changes to past perfect ('he had finished').
questions.hint: Remember to change the question structure to an assertive sentence with 'if' or 'whether'.
questions.subject: maha12-english

questions.question: Choose the correct indirect speech for the given sentence: The tourist exclaimed, "What a magnificent view this is!"

options.text: The tourist exclaimed that that was a magnificent view.
options.explanation: The word 'that' is repeated unnecessarily, making the sentence awkward.

options.text: The tourist exclaimed what a magnificent view that was.
options.explanation: The sentence structure is not grammatically correct for indirect speech.

options.text: The tourist exclaimed with wonder that it was a very magnificent view.
options.explanation: While grammatically correct, this option is unnecessarily wordy compared to option D.

options.text: The tourist exclaimed that it was a very magnificent view.
options.explanation: This option correctly converts the exclamatory sentence into an assertive one, adjusts the pronoun 'this' to 'it', and changes 'is' to 'was'.

questions.explanation: Exclamatory sentences are converted into assertive sentences. 'What a magnificent view this is!' implies great wonder, which can be captured by 'very magnificent'. 'This' changes to 'it' or 'that', and 'is' changes to 'was'. Option D is the most natural and grammatically correct transformation.
questions.hint: Remember to change the exclamatory sentence into an assertive one and adjust the pronouns and determiners.
questions.subject: maha12-english

questions.question: When converting direct speech to indirect speech, the past continuous tense (e.g., "was playing") typically changes to:

options.text: Present Continuous
options.explanation: The tense should change to a form that reflects the past tense of the reporting verb.

options.text: Past Perfect Continuous
options.explanation: This is the correct tense change for past continuous in indirect speech when the reporting verb is in the past.

options.text: Simple Past
options.explanation: The tense change should reflect the duration of the action, which is why past perfect continuous is used.

options.text: Present Perfect Continuous
options.explanation: The tense change should reflect the past tense of the reporting verb.

questions.explanation: According to the rules of narration, if the reporting verb is in the past tense, the past continuous tense in direct speech changes to the past perfect continuous tense in indirect speech.
questions.hint: Recall the rule for changing tenses in indirect speech.
questions.subject: maha12-english

Reason (R): Greetings and wishes are expressed in indirect speech using verbs like 'wished', 'greeted', 'bade', followed by the object and the greeting/wish.

options.explanation: The reason does correctly explain the assertion.

options.explanation: The reason is true and correctly explains the assertion.

questions.explanation: The assertion correctly converts the direct greeting into indirect speech using the appropriate reporting verb 'wished'. The reason accurately explains the rule for converting greetings and wishes, thus providing a correct explanation for the assertion.
questions.hint: Understand the rules for converting greetings and wishes into indirect speech.
questions.subject: maha12-english

questions.question: Read the following dialogue and choose the correct indirect speech conversion: Sunita: "I saw a beautiful peacock in the garden yesterday." Ravi: "Did you take a picture of it?"

options.text: Sunita said that she had seen a beautiful peacock in the garden the day before. Ravi asked if she had taken a picture of it.
options.explanation: This option correctly changes the tenses to past perfect, adjusts the pronouns, and changes 'yesterday' to 'the day before'.

options.text: Sunita said that she saw a beautiful peacock in the garden yesterday. Ravi asked if she took a picture of it.
options.explanation: The tense should change to past perfect ('had seen') because the reporting verb ('said') is in the past.

options.text: Sunita said that she had seen a beautiful peacock in the garden the day before. Ravi asked if she took a picture of it.
options.explanation: The tense in Ravi's part should change to past perfect ('had taken') to match the past tense of the reporting verb.

options.text: Sunita said that I had seen a beautiful peacock in the garden the day before. Ravi asked if she had taken a picture of it.
options.explanation: The pronoun 'I' should change to 'she' as it refers to Sunita in the direct speech.

questions.explanation: In Sunita's statement, 'I saw' (simple past) changes to 'she had seen' (past perfect), and 'yesterday' changes to 'the day before'. In Ravi's question, 'Did you take' (simple past interrogative) changes to 'if she had taken' (past perfect assertive). Pronouns are also correctly adjusted.
questions.hint: Remember to change the tenses and pronouns correctly for both parts of the dialogue.
questions.subject: maha12-english

questions.question: Which of the following expressions correctly replaces "now" in indirect speech?

options.text: Then
options.explanation: This is the standard change for 'now' in indirect speech.

options.text: At present
options.explanation: 'At present' is not the standard replacement for 'now' in indirect speech.

options.text: Currently
options.explanation: 'Currently' is not the standard replacement for 'now' in indirect speech.

options.text: Before
options.explanation: 'Before' does not correctly represent the meaning of 'now' in indirect speech.

questions.explanation: In indirect speech, the adverb of time "now" typically changes to "then."
questions.hint: Recall the standard changes for time expressions in indirect speech.
questions.subject: maha12-english

questions.question: Convert the following sentence into indirect speech: My grandmother often says, "Early to bed, early to rise, makes a man healthy, wealthy, and wise."

options.text: My grandmother often says that early to bed, early to rise, made a man healthy, wealthy, and wise.
options.explanation: The tense should remain unchanged as it is a proverb/universal truth.

options.text: My grandmother often said that early to bed, early to rise, makes a man healthy, wealthy, and wise.
options.explanation: The reporting verb 'says' is in the present tense, so it should not change to 'said'.

options.text: My grandmother often says that early to bed, early to rise, makes a man healthy, wealthy, and wise.
options.explanation: This option correctly retains the present tense of the proverb as the reporting verb is in the present tense.

options.text: My grandmother often says that early to bed, early to rise, would make a man healthy, wealthy, and wise.
options.explanation: The modal 'would' is unnecessary and changes the meaning of the proverb.

questions.explanation: Since the direct speech is a proverb/universal truth and the reporting verb ('says') is in the present tense, there is no change in the tense of the reported speech. Even if the reporting verb were in the past, proverbs and universal truths retain their present tense in indirect speech.
questions.hint: Remember that proverbs and universal truths do not change tense in indirect speech.
questions.subject: maha12-english

questions.question: Choose the correct indirect speech for the given sentence: Direct Speech: 'I will finish my project by tomorrow,' said Rohit.

options.text: Rohit said that he would finish his project by tomorrow.
options.explanation: 'Tomorrow' should change to 'the next day' or 'the following day' in indirect speech.

options.text: Rohit said that he would finish his project by the next day.
options.explanation: Correct conversion of tense ('will' to 'would'), pronoun ('my' to 'his'), and time ('tomorrow' to 'the next day').

options.text: Rohit said that I would finish my project by the next day.
options.explanation: Incorrect pronoun reference; 'I' should be 'he' as it refers to Rohit.

options.text: Rohit said that he will finish his project by the next day.
options.explanation: Incorrect tense usage; 'will' should be 'would' in indirect speech.

questions.explanation: When converting to indirect speech, 'will' changes to 'would', 'my' changes to 'his' (referring to Rohit), and 'tomorrow' changes to 'the next day' or 'the following day'.
questions.hint: Check tense changes and pronoun references.
questions.subject: maha12-english

questions.question: Select the correct indirect speech for the following interrogative sentence: Direct Speech: The librarian asked the student, 'Have you returned the book I lent you last week?'

options.text: The librarian asked the student if he had returned the book he had lent him the previous week.
options.explanation: Correct use of 'if', proper tense change ('have' to 'had'), and accurate pronoun and time reference adjustments.

options.text: The librarian asked the student if you had returned the book she lent him last week.
options.explanation: Incorrect pronoun usage; 'you' should be 'he', and 'I' should change to 'he'/'she'.

options.text: The librarian asked the student that if he had returned the book I lent you the previous week.
options.explanation: Incorrect structure; 'that if' is not standard in indirect speech. Also, pronoun 'I' should be 'he'.

options.text: The librarian asked the student whether he returned the book she had lent him the previous week.
options.explanation: Incorrect tense usage; 'returned' should be 'had returned' (past perfect) to maintain sequence of tenses.

questions.explanation: For interrogative sentences starting with a helping verb, 'if' or 'whether' is used. The tense 'Have returned' (present perfect) changes to 'had returned' (past perfect). Pronouns 'you' and 'I' change to 'he' and 'he'/'she' (depending on context). 'Last week' changes to 'the previous week'.
questions.hint: Remember to use 'if' or 'whether' for yes/no questions and adjust pronouns and tenses accordingly.
questions.subject: maha12-english

questions.question: Identify the correct indirect speech for the given exclamatory sentence: Direct Speech: The tourist exclaimed, 'What a beautiful sunset this is!'

options.text: The tourist exclaimed that what a beautiful sunset that was.
options.explanation: Incorrect structure; exclamatory sentences should be rephrased in assertive form.

options.text: The tourist exclaimed with wonder that it was a very beautiful sunset.
options.explanation: Correct conversion; the exclamation is rephrased as an assertive sentence with appropriate tense and pronoun changes.

options.text: The tourist exclaimed that this was a beautiful sunset.
options.explanation: Incorrect pronoun reference; 'this' should change to 'that' in indirect speech.

options.text: The tourist exclaimed that what a beautiful sunset this is.
options.explanation: Incorrect tense and pronoun usage; no conversion to indirect speech has been done.

questions.explanation: Exclamatory sentences are converted into assertive sentences. 'What a beautiful sunset!' expresses wonder, so 'exclaimed with wonder' is appropriate. 'This' changes to 'that' and 'is' changes to 'was'. The exclamation is rephrased as 'it was a very beautiful sunset'.
questions.hint: Exclamatory sentences often require rephrasing to an assertive form while retaining the expression of emotion.
questions.subject: maha12-english

questions.question: Assertion (A): The sentence 'My mother said, "Honesty is the best policy"' when converted to indirect speech becomes 'My mother said that honesty is the best policy.' Reason (R): When the direct speech expresses a universal truth, a proverb, or a habitual fact, the tense of the verb in the reported speech remains unchanged, even if the reporting verb is in the past tense.

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Both the assertion and reason are correct, and the reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.text: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: The reason is the correct explanation for the assertion.

options.text: A is true but R is false.
options.explanation: Both the assertion and reason are true.

options.text: A is false but R is true.
options.explanation: The assertion is true, and the reason correctly explains it.

questions.explanation: The assertion correctly converts the direct speech to indirect speech without changing the tense of 'is' because 'Honesty is the best policy' is a universal truth/proverb. The reason accurately explains this specific rule of narration, stating that the tense remains unchanged for universal truths/proverbs/habitual facts.
questions.hint: Consider the rules for changing tense in indirect speech, especially for universal truths.
questions.subject: maha12-english

questions.question: Choose the most appropriate indirect speech for the following imperative sentence: Direct Speech: The old man said to the children, 'Please don't pluck the flowers in the garden.'

options.text: The old man requested the children not to pluck the flowers in the garden.
options.explanation: Correct reporting verb ('requested') and accurate conversion of the imperative to indirect speech ('not to pluck').

options.text: The old man told the children that they should not pluck the flowers in the garden.
options.explanation: Incorrect reporting verb ('told' is neutral and does not convey the polite request implied by 'Please').

options.text: The old man ordered the children not to pluck the flowers in the garden.
options.explanation: Incorrect reporting verb ('ordered' conveys a command, not a request).

options.text: The old man advised the children please not to pluck the flowers in the garden.
options.explanation: Incorrect retention of 'please' and inappropriate reporting verb ('advised' does not match the polite tone of 'Please').

questions.explanation: The word 'Please' indicates a request. Therefore, the reporting verb should be 'requested'. The imperative 'Don't pluck' changes to 'not to pluck' in indirect speech. Options B and C use inappropriate reporting verbs for a polite request. Option D incorrectly retains 'please'.
questions.hint: Identify the type of imperative (request, command, advice) and choose the appropriate reporting verb.
questions.subject: maha12-english
